question.text: An investor owns real estate worth Rs. 50 lakh, investments and bank balances of Rs. 10 lakh, and Rs. 5 lakh in provident fund. Outstanding loans include Rs. 10 lakh housing loan, Rs. 2 lakh credit card dues, and Rs. 1 lakh loan from a friend. The leverage ratio is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Total Assets = 50 + 10 + 5 = Rs. 65 lakh. Total Liabilities = 10 + 2 + 1 = Rs. 13 lakh. Leverage Ratio = Total Liabilities / Total Assets = 13/65 = 20%. The Trap: 25% can result from using net worth (Rs. 52 lakh) as the denominator instead of total assets, i.e. 13/52 = 25%. Leverage ratio uses total assets, not net worth. Note: The workbook formula for leverage ratio is total liabilities divided by total assets; a lower ratio indicates lower dependence on borrowed funds.
